title: sw-ml-study typed decision trace
description: What a decision model's run leaves behind: per turn, the state that went in, the choices offered, the typed decisions out, the policy rule that consumed them, and the output that resulted. Renderer-neutral and application-neutral: label names, policy text and output strings are data, never types. Two invariants carry the project's central claim -- there are exactly three decision kinds, and every output string must be exactly one of the candidates the program offered the model -- either the composed candidate a decision selected, or a table frame with deterministically retrieved text spliced into it.

demo.description: Which application produced this trace. A label for the reader; nothing branches on it.

tables.description: Reusable response frames. A turn whose output used the table pattern quotes one of these by index. A trace whose candidates are composed in full may carry no tables at all.

text.description: The unstructured input this turn decided over.

features.description: What the encoder actually saw, for display beside the decision.

memory.description: Structured state the program keeps outside the model.

decision.description: One typed decision. The shape is uniform across all three kinds so one validator, one schema and one renderer serve them all; p and expectation are the only kind-specific fields. selected, confidence and margin are derived from probs and are checked against it, so a trace cannot disagree with itself.

kind.description: There is deliberately no fourth kind. The absence of a generation primitive is the central claim of the project, so it is enforced here.

question.description: The question asked; for a noul, the proposition.

margin.description: Gap between the two most probable labels; 1 for a single-label set. Reported beside confidence because the two are different doubts.

p.description: Noul only: probability that the proposition holds. Equals probs[1].

expectation.description: Scale only: expected level index over the ordered labels.

method.description: "none" for a raw model output, or the name of the map applied.

t.description: The fitted scalar, when the method is a temperature.

rule.description: The rule as written in the application. Thresholds belong to the program, not the model, so they are shown.

output.description: Where the turn's text came from. The invariant is not that output text matches some fixed catalogue; it is that the output is exactly one of the candidates THE PROGRAM offered the model. The model ranks or scores those candidates and does nothing else. Two composition patterns are both legitimate, and a trace declares which it used.

output_table.description: The program chose a frame from a table and spliced deterministically retrieved text into its {} placeholders. text MUST equal that entry with slots filled, in order; an entry with no placeholder must match byte for byte, and the slot count must equal the placeholder count.

slots.description: Values spliced into the frame, in order. These are text the program already had -- retrieved memory, quoted input -- not text any model produced.

output_choice.description: The program built the candidate list as fully-composed strings and the model chose among them. text MUST be byte-identical to the selected label of the decision at the given index.

decision.description: Index into this turn's decisions array.
